desc: A white to gray powdery coating spreads across leaf surfaces and stems, often starting on upper leaf faces, eventually stunting growth and distorting new shoots.
treat: Improve airflow and spacing, remove infected leaves, apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicide at first sign.

desc: Pale yellow blotches appear on upper leaf surfaces with a gray-purple fuzzy growth on the undersides, usually following cool, damp nights.
treat: Avoid overhead watering, increase spacing, apply copper-based fungicide, remove and destroy infected foliage.

desc: Dark brown spots with concentric target-like rings form on lower, older leaves first, surrounded by a yellow halo, and work upward over time.
treat: Remove lower infected leaves, rotate crops yearly, mulch to prevent soil splash, apply chlorothalonil or copper fungicide.

desc: Large, water-soaked, irregular gray-brown blotches spread fast across leaves and stems, often with white fuzzy growth on undersides in wet weather; entire fields can collapse within days.
treat: Destroy infected plants immediately, avoid overhead irrigation, apply protectant fungicide preventatively in high-risk weather, use resistant varieties.

desc: Small raised orange to rust-colored pustules erupt on leaf undersides, leaving a powdery residue on hands or clothing when brushed.
treat: Remove volunteer plants and infected debris, apply triazole or strobilurin fungicide, choose resistant cultivars.

desc: Dark, sunken lesions with concentric rings develop on leaves, stems, and fruit, sometimes oozing pink spore masses in humid conditions.
treat: Prune for airflow, avoid working plants when wet, apply copper or mancozeb fungicide, rotate away from susceptible crops.

desc: A soft brown rot covered in fuzzy gray-brown mold develops on flowers, fruit, and damaged tissue, especially after cool damp periods.
treat: Improve ventilation, remove spent flowers and dying tissue promptly, avoid overhead watering, apply fungicide labeled for Botrytis.

desc: One side of the plant often yellows and wilts first, and a brown discoloration is visible in the stem's vascular tissue when cut lengthwise, even with adequate soil moisture.
treat: Remove and destroy infected plants, solarize soil, rotate to non-host crops for several years, plant resistant varieties — no effective curative fungicide exists.

desc: Lower leaves yellow and wilt in a V-shaped pattern from the leaf margin inward, with brownish streaking in the stem's vascular ring, worsening in cooler weather.
treat: Remove infected plants and roots, rotate with non-host crops for 4+ years, avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties.

desc: Numerous small circular spots with dark margins and tan-gray centers speckle the lower leaves, which yellow and drop as infection climbs the plant.
treat: Remove infected lower leaves, mulch to reduce splash, avoid overhead watering, apply chlorothalonil-based fungicide.

desc: A black, soot-like coating grows on the surface of leaves and stems, following the sugary honeydew left behind by aphids or scale insects rather than infecting tissue directly.
treat: Control the underlying insect pest (aphids, whitefly, scale), wash foliage with mild soapy water to remove residue.

desc: A white cottony growth develops at stem bases or branch junctions, causing sudden wilting; hard black resting bodies (sclerotia) may be visible inside split stems.
treat: Improve spacing and airflow, avoid dense canopy, rotate with grasses, remove infected debris, apply fungicide at flowering in high-risk fields.

desc: Black spots with feathered, irregular margins form on leaves, often surrounded by a yellow halo, leading to early leaf drop on susceptible plants.
treat: Remove fallen infected leaves each season, avoid wetting foliage, apply fungicide on a preventive schedule, prune for airflow.

desc: Grayish-white galls swell on ears, stems, or tassels and rupture to release a mass of powdery black spores as they mature.
treat: Remove and destroy galls before rupture, avoid mechanical wounding of plants, rotate crops, use resistant hybrids.

desc: Raised, corky lesions with water-soaked, yellow-haloed margins erupt on leaves, twigs, and fruit of citrus trees, often coalescing into cracked canker-like patches.
treat: Prune and destroy infected tissue, disinfect tools between cuts, apply copper bactericide sprays, avoid overhead irrigation, use certified disease-free planting stock.

desc: Tissue rapidly breaks down into a slimy, foul-smelling mass, often starting at a wound and spreading through fleshy fruits, tubers, or rhizomes within days.
treat: Remove and destroy affected produce immediately, improve field drainage and storage ventilation, avoid wounding during harvest and handling, store at cool dry temperatures.

desc: Sunken, wrinkled, dry lesions develop on tubers or corms in storage, with internal tissue turning powdery and discolored as the rot progresses inward.
treat: Cure tubers properly before storage, discard damaged or infected stock, maintain cool dry storage conditions, rotate crops and avoid wounding at harvest.

desc: Sunken, discolored lesions girdle the stem at the site of infection, often at a wound or node, eventually cutting off water flow and causing dieback above the canker.
treat: Prune out and destroy cankered stems well below the lesion, disinfect pruning tools, avoid stem wounding, apply protectant fungicide at pruning cuts in high-risk periods.

desc: Bright orange-yellow powdery pustules erupt on the undersides of plumeria leaves, with corresponding yellow blotches on the upper surface, leading to early leaf drop.
treat: Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves, avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation between plants, apply sulfur or copper-based fungicide at first sign.

desc: Individual rice grains are replaced by velvety yellow-green fungal balls that darken to black as they mature, replacing the grain within infected panicles.
treat: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen fertilization, apply fungicide at boot-to-heading stage in high-risk conditions, avoid overly dense planting.

desc: Concentric ring-shaped spots mark the fruit surface while leaves show vein clearing, mottling, and distortion, often accompanied by stunted, misshapen growth of the whole plant.
treat: Remove and destroy infected plants promptly, control aphid vectors, use virus-resistant or tolerant papaya varieties, avoid planting near other infected cucurbits or papaya.

desc: Seedlings collapse suddenly at the soil line shortly after emergence, with a thin, water-soaked, discolored stem lesion, often wiping out entire seed trays or nursery beds.
treat: Improve soil drainage and avoid overwatering, use sterile potting media, avoid overcrowding seedlings, apply a seed treatment or drench fungicide in nursery settings.

desc: Coconut fronds show yellowing and drying from the tip inward, with progressive leaf wilting, stunted new growth, and reduced nut yield over several years, spreading slowly through a plantation.
treat: Remove and destroy severely affected palms to reduce spread, control phloem-feeding insect vectors, avoid moving planting material from affected zones, report suspected cases to local plant protection authorities.

desc: Translucent, oily-looking spots on young tea leaves swell into pale blisters with a white spore layer on the underside, a major disease in Sri Lanka's wet-zone tea estates during monsoon months.
treat: Maintain good field drainage and plucking rounds to reduce leaf wetness duration, apply copper or systemic fungicide on a preventive spray schedule, prune for airflow between bushes.

desc: Rust-orange, velvety circular patches spread across tea leaves and young stems, most common on weak or shaded bushes with poor drainage or nutrition.
treat: Improve drainage and bush nutrition, prune to increase light and airflow, apply copper oxychloride spray on affected sections, avoid excessive shade.

desc: Irregular dark brown to black spots with a distinctive "fishbone" pattern along the leaf midrib and veins cause premature leaf fall in rubber, a serious threat to Sri Lankan rubber plantations.
treat: Use resistant clones where available, apply fungicide during high-risk wet periods, remove and destroy fallen infected leaves, avoid moving planting material from infected estates.

desc: Sudden, heavy defoliation strikes rubber trees during monsoon rains, with black lesions on leaf stalks and pods causing green, unshed leaves and pods to drop together.
treat: Apply protectant fungicide sprays before and during the monsoon season, improve field drainage, avoid planting in low-lying waterlogged areas, remove fallen infected material.

desc: A pinkish, cobweb-like fungal growth encircles branches and stems of rubber trees, girdling the bark and causing wilting and dieback of everything above the infected point.
treat: Prune and destroy infected branches well below the pink growth, apply fungicidal paste to pruning wounds, improve canopy spacing and airflow, avoid excess shade and humidity.

desc: The unopened spear leaf at the crown rots and can be pulled out easily, releasing a foul odor, while surrounding fronds yellow and droop — often fatal to the palm if not caught early.
treat: Remove and burn severely affected palms, apply copper fungicide to the crown of neighboring at-risk palms, improve drainage around the base, avoid crown injury during maintenance.

desc: A reddish-brown to black rot develops at the base of the coconut trunk, with fronds yellowing and drooping progressively over months to years as the internal tissue decays.
treat: Remove and destroy severely infected palms including stumps and roots, avoid replanting coconut in the same spot immediately, improve drainage, isolate healthy palms with trenching where feasible.

desc: Diamond-shaped spots with gray centers and brown margins form on leaves, and infection at the neck node can snap the panicle entirely, one of the most damaging rice diseases in Sri Lanka.
treat: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen fertilization, maintain proper water management, apply fungicide at tillering and booting stages in high-risk conditions.

desc: Water-soaked streaks starting at leaf tips or margins turn yellow-white and expand into wavy-edged blighted patches, spreading rapidly during warm, wet, windy weather.
treat: Use resistant varieties and certified disease-free seed, avoid excess nitrogen, maintain balanced water levels, avoid field work when leaves are wet, remove infected stubble after harvest.

desc: Irregular, greenish-gray lesions with brown borders form on the leaf sheath near the waterline, climbing upward in dense, humid stands and reducing grain fill.
treat: Avoid overly dense planting and excess nitrogen, maintain good field drainage between irrigations, apply fungicide at panicle initiation in high-risk fields, rotate with non-host crops.

desc: Black pepper vines wilt and collapse rapidly, sometimes within days, with blackened, rotted roots and a water-soaked lesion girdling the stem base — a major cause of vine loss in Sri Lankan pepper cultivation.
treat: Improve drainage around vine bases, avoid waterlogging during monsoon, apply Bordeaux mixture or systemic fungicide as a preventive drench, remove and destroy collapsed vines promptly.

desc: Chlorotic streaks run parallel to leaf veins on cardamom, with leaves becoming narrow, distorted, and mottled as the whole plant becomes progressively stunted and unproductive.
treat: Rogue and destroy infected clumps immediately, control aphid vectors, use virus-tested planting material, avoid taking suckers from symptomatic clumps.

desc: Small brown spots with darker margins appear scattered across cinnamon leaves, enlarging and merging in prolonged wet weather to cause premature leaf drop and weakened shoots.
treat: Prune for airflow and remove fallen infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, apply copper-based fungicide during wet periods, maintain balanced fertilization.

desc: Roots develop numerous small knotty galls that disrupt water and nutrient uptake, causing stunting, yellowing, and wilting in hot weather even when soil moisture is adequate.
treat: Rotate with non-host crops such as marigold or grasses, solarize soil before planting, use resistant varieties where available, avoid moving infested soil or seedlings between plots.

desc: Roots rot and turn reddish-black internally, weakening the plant’s anchorage until top-heavy, fruiting banana plants topple over, often without warning.
treat: Use clean, nematode-free planting material (tissue-cultured plants where possible), rotate out of banana for a season, apply nematicide or organic soil amendments, remove and destroy fallen mats.

desc: Pepper vines decline slowly over one or more seasons, with yellowing leaves, thinning foliage, and reduced vigor as damaged roots lose their ability to support the plant.
treat: Use certified nematode-free planting material, improve soil organic matter, apply nematicide to the root zone where infestation is confirmed, avoid replanting immediately in heavily infested beds.

desc: Citrus trees decline gradually with smaller leaves, twig dieback, and reduced fruit size over several years — often mistaken for nutrient deficiency since there is no single dramatic symptom.
treat: Test soil for nematode presence before planting new citrus, use tolerant rootstocks, maintain good irrigation and nutrition to reduce stress, apply nematicide where populations are high.

desc: The tips of young leaves, especially the flag leaf, turn white or pale and twist, and affected panicles are often sterile or poorly filled — the nematode spreads mainly through infected seed.
treat: Use certified, nematode-free seed, hot-water treat seed before sowing where infestation is suspected, rotate with non-host crops, avoid saving seed from affected fields.

desc: Plants grow poorly in patches across the field, with yellowing and wilting foliage in circular zones; tiny cysts are visible on the roots when dug up, common in Sri Lanka’s cooler upcountry potato land.
treat: Rotate with non-host crops for several years, use certified cyst-free seed potatoes, avoid moving infested soil between fields on tools or footwear, use resistant varieties where available.
